title: 86-style static code decomposition into state / operation / law / time / memory / feedback
method: Lexical scan of each reference style source + REA semantic graph. Static only: nothing executed, no source text stored here.
evidence: E2_STATIC_CODE (labels inferred from code patterns; not a render test)

shared_code_lineage.meaning: REA normalized-AST fingerprints (functions of 3+ lines) that appear in more than one style: these styles reuse the same drawing routine, so pairing them is not an independent combination.

findings.pure_function_of_time: All 86 styles are written as frame = f(t); none keeps state between frames.
findings.memory_is_simulated: 3/86 styles fake history by recomputing earlier t inside the frame (trail_by_resampling); no style stores a material memory that later frames read.
findings.temporal_feedback_styles: 0/86: no style carries pixels or state from one frame into the next (every frame is rebuilt from t).
findings.implication: A persistent memory field that changes later motion (the glass-memory recipe) is a mechanism the 86 references do not contain; it must be simulated outside the pure-t frame and played back.
